back: The arrangement of nodes and links in a network.
All devices share one backbone with a terminator at each end; cheap, but collisions and a backbone fault affects everything.
Each device has its own cable to a central switch; one cable fault affects one device, a switch fault affects all.
Links = n(n − 1) ÷ 2; each device needs n − 1 ports.
A combination of topologies, for example stars linked by a backbone.
The weakening of a signal as it travels along a medium.
Pulses of light; very high bandwidth; very low attenuation; immune to electromagnetic interference; costly.
Microwave: narrow beam in line of sight over tens of kilometres. Satellite: wide coverage, remote areas, longer delay, costly.
